title: The Happy Prince
author: Oscar Wilde
summary: 伫立在城市高处的快乐王子雕像与一只南飞的小燕子相遇，为了救济苦难的底层穷人，王子舍弃了身上的黄金宝石与蓝宝石双眸，小燕子留下了最后的温暖，最终双双升入天堂。

paragraphs.author: Oscar Wilde (王尔德)
paragraphs.en:
The Happy Prince
Oscar Wilde (王尔德)
paragraphs.zh: 《快乐王子》 · Oscar Wilde (王尔德)

paragraphs.en: High above the city, on a tall column, stood the statue of the Happy Prince. He was gilded all over with thin leaves of fine gold, for eyes he had two bright sapphires, and a large red ruby glowed on his sword-hilt.
paragraphs.zh: 在城市的上空，高耸的圆柱上立着快乐王子的雕像。他浑身贴满纯金薄片，双眼是两颗明亮的蓝宝石，剑柄上一颗硕大的红宝石闪闪发光。

paragraphs.en: He was very much admired indeed. 'He is as beautiful as a weathercock,' remarked one of the Town Councillors; 'only not quite so useful,' he added, fearing lest people should think him unpractical.
paragraphs.zh: 他深受人们的赞美。“他像风向标一样漂亮，”一位市镇议员评论道，唯恐别人觉得自己不切实际，他又补充了一句：“只是没有风向标那么实用罢了。”

paragraphs.en: 'Why can't you be like the Happy Prince?' asked a sensible mother of her little boy who was crying for the moon. 'The Happy Prince never dreams of crying for anything.'
paragraphs.zh: “你为什么不能学学快乐王子呢？”一位明理的母亲问她哭着要摘月亮的小男孩，“快乐王子无论想要什么，都从不哭闹。”

paragraphs.en: 'I am glad there is someone in the world who is quite happy,' muttered a disappointed man as he gazed at the wonderful statue.
paragraphs.zh: “很高兴这世上竟还有如此快乐的人，”一位心灰意冷的人仰望着这尊奇妙的雕像喃喃自语。

paragraphs.en: One night there flew over the city a little Swallow. His friends had gone away to Egypt six weeks before, but he had stayed behind, for he was in love with the most beautiful Reed.
paragraphs.zh: 一天夜里，一只小燕子飞过城市上空。他的伙伴们六个星期前就飞去埃及了，但他留了下来，因为他爱上了一株最美丽的芦苇。

paragraphs.en: 'Shall I love you?' said the Swallow, who liked to come to the point at once, and the Reed made him a low bow. So he flew round and round her, touching the water with his wings and making silver ripples.
paragraphs.zh: “我能爱你吗？”直爽的小燕子问道，芦苇向他深深地鞠了一躬。于是小燕子绕着她飞了一圈又一圈，羽翼轻拂水面，荡起阵阵银色的涟漪。

paragraphs.en: All through the summer he stayed, but as autumn came the other swallows were far away. 'She has no conversation,' said the Swallow, 'and I am afraid she is a coquette, for she is always flirting with the wind.'
paragraphs.zh: 他留下来度过了整个夏天。但随着秋天来临，伙伴们早已远去。“她不会交谈，”小燕子叹息道，“而且我担心她是个轻浮的姑娘，因为她总是迎着风眉目传情。”

paragraphs.en: So when all was over he said to her, 'Will you come away with me?' But the Reed shook her head; she was too attached to her home. 'You have been trifling with my love,' he cried. 'I am off to the Pyramids. Good-bye!'
paragraphs.zh: 于是当一切归于平静，他问芦苇：“你愿意跟我走吗？”芦苇摇了摇头，她太留恋自己的家乡了。“你一直在玩弄我的感情，”小燕子哭喊道，“我要去金字塔了。再见吧！”

paragraphs.en: All day long he flew, and at night-time he arrived at the city. 'Where shall I put up?' he said; 'I hope the town has made preparations.' Then he saw the statue on the tall column.
paragraphs.zh: 他飞了一整天，直到夜晚才飞抵这座城市。“我在哪儿过夜呢？”他说，“希望城里已经做好了准备。”这时，他看见了高柱上的雕像。

paragraphs.en: 'I will put up there,' he cried; 'it is a fine position with plenty of fresh air.' So he alighted just between the feet of the Happy Prince. 'I have a golden bedroom,' he whispered softly to himself.
paragraphs.zh: “我就住在那儿吧，”他喊道，“那是个绝佳的位置，空气很清新。”于是他在快乐王子的两只脚之间落下了脚。“我有一间金色的卧室，”他轻声对自己低语。

paragraphs.en: Just as he was putting his head under his wing a large drop of water fell on him. 'What a curious thing!' he cried; 'there is not a single cloud in the sky, the stars are quite clear and bright, and yet it is raining.'
paragraphs.zh: 正当他把小脑袋缩进翅膀下面准备入睡时，一大滴水珠落在他身上。“真奇怪！”他叫道，“天上连一丝云彩都没有，星星闪烁澄澈，居然会下雨。”

paragraphs.en: Then another drop fell. 'What is the use of a statue if it cannot keep the rain off?' he said. 'I must look for a good chimney-pot.' But before he had opened his wings, a third drop fell, and he looked up, and saw—Ah! what did he see?
paragraphs.zh: 接着又落下一滴水。“一尊连雨都遮挡不住的雕像，要它何用？”他说，“我得找个好烟囱去。”可还没等他展开双翅，第三滴水又落了下来。他抬起头一看——啊！他看见了什么？

paragraphs.en: The eyes of the Happy Prince were filled with tears, and tears were running down his golden cheeks. His face was so beautiful in the moonlight that the little Swallow was filled with pity.
paragraphs.zh: 快乐王子的双眼盈满了泪水，颗颗泪珠顺着金色的脸庞滚滚滑落。月光下他的脸容是如此美丽高洁，小燕子心里充满了怜悯。

paragraphs.en: 'Who are you?' he said. 'I am the Happy Prince.' 'Why are you weeping then?' asked the Swallow; 'you have quite drenched me.'
paragraphs.zh: “你是谁？”小燕子问。“我是快乐王子。”“那你为什么哭泣呢？”小燕子问，“你把我都全淋湿了。”

paragraphs.en: 'When I was alive and had a human heart,' answered the statue, 'I did not know what tears were, for I lived in the Palace of Sans-Souci, where sorrow is not allowed to enter.'
paragraphs.zh: “当我活着拥有一颗人类的心脏时，”雕像回答，“我不知道眼泪为何物，因为我住在无忧宫里，悲哀与忧愁被严禁入内。”

paragraphs.en: 'In the daytime I played with my companions in the garden, and in the evening I led the dance in the Great Hall. Round the garden ran a very lofty wall, but I never cared to ask what lay beyond it, everything about me was so beautiful.'
paragraphs.zh: “白天我和伙伴们在花园里嬉戏，晚上在大厅里领舞。花园周围筑有一道高高的围墙，但我从不在意墙外究竟是什么，因为我身边的一切都是如此美好。”

paragraphs.en: 'My courtiers called me the Happy Prince, and happy indeed I was, if pleasure be happiness. So I lived, and so I died. And now that I am dead they have set me up here so high that I can see all the ugliness and all the misery of my city.'
paragraphs.zh: “朝臣们都叫我‘快乐王子’。如果享乐就算是快乐的话，那我确实快乐。我就这样活着，就这样死去。现在我死了，他们却把我高高地立在这里，让我饱览整座城市里所有的丑恶与苦难。”

paragraphs.en: 'And though my heart is made of lead yet I cannot choose but weep.' 'What! is he not solid gold?' said the Swallow to himself. He was too polite to make any personal remarks out loud.
paragraphs.zh: “即使我的心是铅铸的，我也忍不住要哭泣。”“什么！难道他不是通体纯金的？”小燕子自言自语道。他很有教养，没有大声对私人问题品头论足。

paragraphs.en: 'Far away,' continued the statue in a low musical voice, 'far away in a little street there is a poor house. One of the windows is open, and through it I can see a woman seated at a table. Her face is thin and worn, and she has coarse, red hands, all pricked by the needle, for she is a seamstress.'
paragraphs.zh: “在遥远的地方，”雕像用低沉悦耳的声音继续说道，“在一条狭窄的小街深处有一户贫寒的人家。一扇窗子敞开着，透过窗户我看见一个妇人坐在桌旁。她的面容消瘦憔悴，双手粗糙通红，布满了针眼，因为她是一位女裁缝。”

paragraphs.en: 'In a bed in the corner of the room her little boy is lying ill. He has a fever, and is asking for oranges. His mother has nothing to give him but river water, so he is crying. Swallow, Swallow, little Swallow, will you not bring her the ruby out of my sword-hilt?'
paragraphs.zh: “在屋角的小床上，她的小男孩正病倒在床。他发着高烧，直吵着要吃橘子。他的母亲除了河水什么也拿不出来，所以孩子一直在哭泣。燕子，燕子，小燕子，你愿意把我剑柄上的红宝石取下来送给她吗？”

paragraphs.en: 'I am waited for in Egypt,' said the Swallow. 'My friends are flying up and down the Nile, and talking to the large lotus-flowers. Soon they will go to sleep in the tomb of the great King.'
paragraphs.zh: “伙伴们在埃及等我呢，”小燕子说，“我的朋友们正在尼罗河上下飞翔，和硕大的莲花闲聊。很快他们就要到伟大法老的陵墓里安睡了。”

paragraphs.en: 'Swallow, Swallow, little Swallow,' said the Prince, 'will you not stay with me for one night, and be my messenger? The boy is so thirsty, and the mother so sad.'
paragraphs.zh: “燕子，燕子，小燕子，”王子说，“你不能陪我留宿一个夜晚，做我的信使吗？孩子渴得厉害，母亲又那么伤心。”

paragraphs.en: The Happy Prince looked so sad that the little Swallow was sorry. 'It is very cold here,' he said; 'but I will stay with you for one night, and be your messenger.' 'Thank you, little Swallow,' said the Prince.
paragraphs.zh: 快乐王子看起来是那么哀伤，小燕子心软了。“这里非常冷，”小燕子说，“但我愿意陪你待一个夜晚，做你的信使。”“谢谢你，小燕子，”王子答道。

paragraphs.en: So the Swallow picked out the great ruby from the Prince's sword, and flew away with it in his beak over the roofs of the town. He passed by the cathedral tower, where the white marble angels were sculptured.
paragraphs.zh: 于是小燕子啄下了王子剑柄上的大红宝石，衔在嘴里，飞越小镇的座座屋顶。他掠过了雕刻着白色大理石天使的大教堂高塔。

paragraphs.en: At last he came to the poor house and looked in. The boy was tossing feverishly on his bed, and the mother had fallen asleep, she was so tired. In he hopped, and laid the great ruby on the table beside the woman's thimble.
paragraphs.zh: 终于，他来到了那间贫穷的小屋，朝里面望去。发烧的男孩在床上辗转反侧，疲惫不堪的母亲已沉沉睡去。小燕子跳进屋里，把那颗硕大的红宝石轻轻放在女人的顶针旁。

paragraphs.en: Then he flew gently round the bed, fanning the boy's forehead with his wings. 'How cool I feel,' said the boy, 'I must be getting better'; and he sank into a delicious slumber.
paragraphs.zh: 接着，他轻轻绕着病床飞翔，用羽翼为男孩的前额扇动清风。“好凉爽啊，”男孩喃喃道，“我一定快要好起来了。”随即陷入了甜美的梦乡。

paragraphs.en: Then the Swallow flew back to the Happy Prince, and told him what he had done. 'It is curious,' he remarked, 'but I feel quite warm now, although it is so cold.' 'That is because you have done a good action,' said the Prince.
paragraphs.zh: 小燕子飞回快乐王子身边，告诉了他所做的一切。“真奇妙，”小燕子说，“虽然天气这么冷，我现在却觉得浑身暖洋洋的。”“那是因为你做了一件善事，”王子微笑着说。

paragraphs.en: When day broke he flew down to the river and had a bath. 'To-night I go to Egypt,' said the Swallow, and he was in high spirits at the prospect. But as night fell, the Prince begged him to stay another night.
paragraphs.zh: 天亮之后，小燕子飞到河边洗了个澡。“今晚我就动身去埃及！”小燕子满怀憧憬，精神振奋。可当夜幕再次降临，王子又恳求他再陪伴自己一个夜晚。

paragraphs.en: 'Far away across the city,' said the Prince, 'I see a young man in a garret. He is leaning over a desk covered with papers, and in a tumbler by his side there is a bunch of withered violets. He is trying to finish a play for the Director of the Theatre, but he is too cold to write any more.'
paragraphs.zh: “在城市的另一端，”王子说，“我看见阁楼里有一个年轻的男子。他伏在堆满稿纸的书桌上，身旁的水杯里插着一束凋零的紫罗兰。他正拼命想为剧院经理赶写一部剧作，可他冻得再也写不下去了。”

paragraphs.en: 'Take one of my eyes,' said the Prince, 'which are made of rare sapphires, and carry it to him. He will sell it to the jeweller, and buy firewood, and finish his play.' So the Swallow plucked out the Prince's sapphire eye, and flew away to the student's garret.
paragraphs.zh: “把我的一只眼睛取下来吧，”王子说，“那是珍贵的稀世蓝宝石，把它送给他。他可以卖给珠宝商换取柴火和面包，写完他的剧作。”于是小燕子啄下了王子的一只蓝宝石眼睛，飞向穷学生的阁楼。

paragraphs.en: The next night the Prince gave away his other sapphire eye to save a poor little match-girl whose matches had fallen into the gutter. Now the Prince was completely blind.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天夜里，王子又把另一只蓝宝石眼睛献给了一个可怜的卖火柴的小女孩，因为她的火柴全掉进了阴沟里。现在，快乐王子彻底双目失明了。

paragraphs.en: 'You are blind now,' said the Swallow, 'so I will stay with you always.' And the little Swallow slept at the Prince's feet, and told him stories of strange lands.
paragraphs.zh: “你现在双眼失明了，”小燕子紧挨着他说，“所以我要永远留下来陪着你。”从此，小燕子就睡在王子的脚边，每天为他讲述遥远异国的神奇故事。

paragraphs.en: Then the frost came. The poor little Swallow grew colder and colder, but he would not leave the Prince, he loved him too well. At last he knew that he was going to die. 'Goodbye, dear Prince!' he murmured.
paragraphs.zh: 随后严冬与白霜降临了。可怜的小燕子越来越冷、越来越虚弱，但他绝不肯离开王子，他太深爱他了。最后，他知道自己即将死去了。“再见了，亲爱的王子！”他虚弱地呢喃道。

paragraphs.en: He kissed the Happy Prince on the lips, and fell down dead at his feet. At that moment a curious crack sounded inside the statue, as if something had broken. The leaden heart had snapped right in two.
paragraphs.zh: 他在快乐王子的唇上轻轻印下一吻，便跌落在他的脚下死去了。就在那一刻，雕像内部传来一声奇特的破裂声，仿佛有什么东西碎了。那颗铅铸的心脏，彻底裂成了两半。
